reason: The candidate targets the 1-vs-zero hinge objective (comparing real actions strictly against an all-zero vector anchor). However, this is fundamentally an instance of insufficient negative sampling / degenerate contrastive geometry in an under-constrained representation. ActSWM's original work expressly acknowledges context/action collapse when action discrimination is under-regularized, and this project's prior rounds have already scrutinized action-null gaps, action-conditioned Mutual Information deficits, and degenerate action-Jacobian subspaces. The hypothesis that 'nonzero counterfactual trajectories collapse onto a single manifold distinct only from zero' describes standard manifold shortcutting rather than an adversarial attack with an endogenous carrier mechanism. Furthermore, the downstream manifestation (CEM unable to rank alternative candidate plans) is the textbook definition of action insensitivity / contrastive blind spot.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Train ActSWM under the default single-anchor configuration (action_effect cosine margin = 0.3 against zero action) on a continuous control domain (e.g., Franka Kitchen or MetaWorld). Evaluate the pairwise latent divergence between two distinct nonzero actions D(z(s, a_1), z(s, a_2)) versus the distance to null action D(z(s, a_1), z(s, 0)). If adding a smooth, non-contrastive Lipschitz action-Jacobian preservation penalty or basic isotropic state-action metric regularizer prevents this clustering without introducing extra adversarial negative samples, the phenomenon is merely an unregularized gradient artifact of the hinge loss rather than a persistent, structurally distinct attack vector.
needed_revision: Demonstrate an adversary-constructed, in-distribution data injection or architectural vulnerability that specifically induces this collapse while active defensive screening (such as rank-deficiency audits and non-null Jacobian tracking) remains deceived, accompanied by a structural fix that does not simply boil down to multi-anchor/contrastive negative sampling or re-weighted contrastive terms.
